questions.question: In which year did the Indian Constitution declare Hindi in Devanagari script to be the official language of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1949**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindi in Devanagari script** was declared the official language of the Union of India in **1949**.
 
• This declaration is enshrined in **Article 343** of the Constitution of India.
 
• According to this article, Hindi in Devanagari script would be used for official purposes of the Union, while the international form of Indian numerals would be used for official purposes.
 
• The Constituent Assembly adopted this provision on **14th September 1949**, which is now celebrated as **Hindi Diwas** every year.
 
• The Constitution also allowed for the continued use of English for official purposes for a period of 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution, which could be extended by legislation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in Article 368.

questions.question: After being passed by both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, the Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2023 received the President’s assent on ________ to become the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was passed by both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha before receiving the President's assent.
 
• The President's assent was given on **Tue Apr 11 2023 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**, making it the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.
 
• The Act introduces several changes aimed at enhancing the effectiveness of the Competition Commission of India (CCI).
 
• These amendments are expected to improve the regulatory framework and ensure a fair competitive environment in the market.
 
• The Act also includes provisions to simplify the procedure for approval of mergers and acquisitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Competition Commission of India (CCI) is the regulatory body responsible for enforcing the Competition Act, 2002.
 
• The amendments are part of ongoing efforts to align the Act with changing economic conditions and international best practices.
 
• The Act covers various aspects of anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, and regulation of combinations.
 
• Stakeholders have broadly welcomed the amendments, noting that they will contribute to a more robust and dynamic economic environment.

questions.question: What is the wavelength range of visible light ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.4 to 0.7 µm**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The wavelength range of **visible light** is typically from **0.4 to 0.7 µm** (micrometers).
 
• This range corresponds to the colors violet (at the shortest wavelength) to red (at the longest wavelength) within the visible spectrum.
 
• Visible light is the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum that is detectable by the human eye.
 
• Wavelengths shorter than 0.4 µm fall into the ultraviolet range, while wavelengths longer than 0.7 µm fall into the infrared range.
 
• Understanding the wavelength range of visible light is crucial in fields such as optics, photography, and astronomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isaac Newton** was one of the first scientists to study the properties of light and to demonstrate that white light could be split into its component colors using a prism.
 
• The study of light and its interactions is known as **optics**, a branch of physics.
 
• The visible spectrum is just a small part of the entire electromagnetic spectrum, which includes other types of waves such as radio waves, microwaves, X-rays, and gamma rays.
 
• Technological applications that utilize the visible light spectrum include **LED lighting, fiber optics, and lasers**.
 
• The concept of wavelength is essential in understanding phenomena such as diffraction, interference, and the Doppler effect.

questions.question: A _______ is issued to prevent an inferior court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction, which is not legally vested, or acting without jurisdiction or acting against the principles of natural justice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**writ of prohibition**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **writ of prohibition** is issued to prevent an inferior court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction, which is not legally vested, or acting without jurisdiction or acting against the principles of natural justice.
 
• This writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to stop them from doing something that exceeds their jurisdiction.
 
• The writ of prohibition is a judicial order that ensures that the lower courts do not overstep their boundaries and adhere to the principles of natural justice.
 
• It is preventive in nature and issued before the trial or decision is made by the lower court or tribunal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Writ of Habeas Corpus:** This writ is used to bring a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court to determine if the detention is legal.
 
• **Writ of Mandamus:** This writ commands a public official, government agency, or lower court to perform a duty they are legally obligated to complete.
 
• **Writ of Quo-Warranto:** This writ challenges the legality of a person’s claim to a public office.
 
• The **Constitution of India** provides for the issuance of these writs under Article 32 and Article 226 to protect the fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• The power to issue writs is vested in the Supreme Court and the High Courts of India.

questions.question: The reaction of an acid and a metal gives :

options.text: carbon dioxide, salt and hydrogen gas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hydrogen gas and salt**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between an acid and a metal produces **hydrogen gas and salt**.
 
• This type of reaction is a common example of a single displacement reaction where the metal displaces hydrogen from the acid.
 
• The general equation for this reaction is:

 **Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen gas**.
 
• For example, when zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid, zinc chloride and hydrogen gas are produced:

 **Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Not all metals react with acids to produce hydrogen gas. For example, copper does not react with dilute hydrochloric acid.
 
• The reactivity of a metal with an acid depends on its position in the reactivity series. Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series will typically displace hydrogen from acids.
 
• Safety note: Hydrogen gas is flammable, and care should be taken to avoid ignition sources when performing such reactions.

questions.question: In India, statutory liquidity ratio is fixed by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** (RBI) is responsible for fixing the statutory liquidity ratio (SLR) in India.
 
• SLR is a requirement that mandates commercial banks to maintain a certain percentage of their net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) in the form of liquid assets such as cash, gold, or government-approved securities.
 
• The primary objective of SLR is to ensure the solvency of banks and control the expansion of credit.
 
• By adjusting the SLR, the RBI can influence the liquidity and credit growth in the banking system.
 
• SLR is one of the monetary policy tools used by the RBI to manage inflation and ensure financial stability in the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** was established on **1st April 1935** and nationalized on **1st January 1949**.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• It regulates the issue and supply of the Indian rupee and oversees the country's main payment systems.
 
• The RBI also manages the country's foreign exchange and monetary policy.
 
• In addition to SLR, the RBI uses various other tools like the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Repo Rate, and Reverse Repo Rate to regulate the money supply and maintain economic stability.

questions.question: What enables IoT devices to gather data and exchange it over the network?

• Sensors collect data from the environment, such as temperature, humidity, and motion, while actuators perform actions based on the data received, such as turning on a light or adjusting a thermostat.
 
• These components allow IoT devices to interact with their surroundings and communicate the collected data to other devices or centralized systems for processing and analysis.
 
• The integration of sensors and actuators with network connectivity forms the backbone of IoT systems, facilitating automation and real-time monitoring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IoT (Internet of Things)** refers to the network of physical objects embedded with sensors, software, and other technologies to connect and exchange data with other devices and systems over the internet.
 
• The concept of IoT has various applications, including smart homes, healthcare, industrial automation, and environmental monitoring.
 
• Data collected by IoT devices can be used for predictive maintenance, improving efficiency, and enhancing user experiences.
 
• Ensuring data security and privacy is a significant challenge in IoT implementations, necessitating robust encryption and authentication mechanisms.
